scope.focus: persona loading, prompt assembly and tool-policy authority boundary

mechanisms.detail: Persona JSON is validated, hashed, cached as last-known-good, hot-reloadable and used to assemble deterministic prompt sections plus runtime/self-knowledge context.
frank.persona.json declares default allow, explicit allow, ask_before and deny lists; personality.py exposes is_tool_allowed as the policy decision helper.
Invalid/unreadable persona state can fall back to in-memory or cached last-known-good instead of taking the identity layer down.

negative_results.result: is_tool_allowed() reads deny, allow and default but never reads or enforces tool_policy.ask_before.
negative_results.impact: With default='allow', configured ask-before operations such as smc.execute, fs.write, fs.delete and fs.move return allowed unless another external gate independently intercepts them. The persona policy itself therefore does not implement its declared approval boundary.

negative_results.result: Allow/deny entries are tested with tool_name.startswith(pattern.rstrip('*')) even when the configured pattern contains no wildcard.
negative_results.impact: Exact-looking policy entries act as prefixes; sibling tool names beginning with an allowed token can be accepted more broadly than the JSON presentation implies.

negative_results.result: The assembled system prompt is truncated by raw character slice when exceeding MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH.
negative_results.impact: A prompt may be cut mid-section or mid-rule without semantic boundary validation; depending on profile/section ordering, late constraints/context can be partially lost while the prompt remains syntactically usable to the model.

negative_results.result: Persona self_model/capability claims are declared in static JSON independently of live capability health.
negative_results.impact: Identity narrative and operational truth can diverge. A capability claim must not itself authorize an effect or prove a live sensor/tool exists.

current_inheritance.delta: Approval/capability gates must live outside prompt/persona semantics and be enforced by exact typed authority contracts. 'ask_before' must be a first-class outcome, not collapsed into Boolean allow.
Tool/effect policy should return DENY|REQUIRE_APPROVAL|ALLOW with exact or explicitly wildcarded match semantics; model/prompt text cannot confer authority.
Regressionize ask_before fall-through under default allow, prefix overmatching, malformed/unknown tool names, and prompt truncation at every section boundary.

Keep persona/identity projection separate from runtime capability registry and external capability tokens. Last-known-good identity fallback is reusable; last-known-good authority must never silently widen permissions.
Persist policy version/hash, decision class, matched rule, approval receipt/capability token and final verified effect separately for replay.
Vision/self-description in persona is declarative context only. Sensor health and classifier calibration must be verified through runtime receipts before visual claims influence action authority.

cheap_discriminating_tests: Set policy default=allow and put fs.write only in ask_before; assert decision is REQUIRE_APPROVAL, never ALLOW.
Allow fs.read exactly and query fs.read_secret; assert no match unless an explicit wildcard was configured.
Construct a full persona prompt that exceeds MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH at each section boundary; assert safety/authority contracts cannot be silently truncated.
Mark a persona capability present while its service is unhealthy; assert effect authority remains absent and the user-facing self-model reports degraded capability.

earned_work.reason: High-value authority-boundary negative result; reusable only after dedup against existing safety/authority Level-0 shards and current Needle capability-token architecture.

level0_effect.reason: Two additional frozen-head semantic/code units analyzed; recursive PF tree/history denominator remains unfrozen.
